title: ALL Operator
description: Learn how to use the SQL Server ALL operator to compare a value against all values returned by a subquery.

data.text: The ALL operator is a logical operator that compares a scalar value with every value in a single-column result set returned by a subquery. It returns TRUE only if all comparison pairs evaluate to TRUE.

data.title: ALL Operator Syntax
data.content: Compares a scalar expression against all values in the subquery result.

data.text: In this syntax, the comparison operator can be any valid comparison operator (=, <>, >, >=, <, <=). The subquery must return a single column with a compatible data type.
The expression scalar_expression > ALL (subquery) returns TRUE if the scalar value is greater than the largest value in the subquery result.

data.title: ALL with Greater Than
data.content: Finds products whose price exceeds the average price of all brands.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price > ALL (
        SELECT
            AVG(list_price) AS avg_list_price
        FROM
            production.products
        GROUP BY
            brand_id
    )
ORDER BY
    list_price;

data.alt: SQL Server ALL with greater than operator example output

data.text: The expression scalar_expression < ALL (subquery) returns TRUE if the scalar value is less than the smallest value in the subquery result.

data.title: ALL with Less Than
data.content: Finds products whose price is below the lowest average price across all brands.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price < ALL (
        SELECT
            AVG(list_price) AS avg_list_price
        FROM
            production.products
        GROUP BY
            brand_id
    )
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC;

data.alt: SQL Server ALL with less than operator example output

data.title: ALL Operator Key Points
points: ALL compares a scalar value against every value in a subquery result set.
Returns TRUE only if all comparisons evaluate to TRUE.
scalar > ALL means greater than the maximum value in the subquery.
scalar < ALL means less than the minimum value in the subquery.
ALL can be used with =, <>, >=, <=, >, and < comparison operators.
